name: MCP reference servers
works_with: Claude Desktop and other MCP apps
short: Official example MCP servers for files, memory, web fetching, git and more.
what: A small set of official example MCP servers: Everything, Fetch, Filesystem, Git, Memory, Sequential Thinking and Time. They give an AI app tools like reading files, fetching web pages or keeping a memory.
who: Developers learning MCP or building their own servers. Non-developers can still use Memory, Fetch or Filesystem by pasting a config block into Claude Desktop. For a full list of servers, the README points to the MCP Registry at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.
needs: Node.js (for the `npx` servers) or `uv` (for the Python servers). The README doesn't give versions
An MCP app. Claude Desktop is the example the README uses
No accounts or keys for the core servers

steps.title: Try a server on its own
steps.text: This runs the Memory server. On its own it isn't very useful; the next step plugs it into your AI app.

watch: The README says these are reference implementations, not production-ready servers.
Many well-known servers (GitHub, Slack, Postgres, Puppeteer, Google Drive and others) have been archived. The README's example config still shows GitHub and Postgres, so skip those.
Filesystem gives your AI read and write access to the folder you list. Point it at one specific folder, never your whole home folder.
